title: Bible Graph — book source file
description: One source file per Bible book. Nodes carry their own incoming prerequisite edges (the edge lives with the dependent node). Compiled by scripts/build.mjs into dist/nodes.json and dist/edges.json.

domain.description: Default domain for nodes in this book; a node may override it.

id.description: Stable slug, e.g. gen-1-3, rom-8, ps-110, wis-1-9.

chapters.description: Chapter numbers covered. Strings allowed for special units (e.g. "Additions A-F" in Greek Esther).

domain.description: Override of the book-level domain for mixed-genre books.

difficulty_tier.description: How hard this passage is to UNDERSTAND, 1 (entry level) to 5 (hardest). This is intrinsic difficulty, NOT position in the graph — a node may sit deep in the prerequisite chain and still be easy to read (Revelation 21-22), or sit early and be hard (Job). For 'what is a reader ready for', use the derived prerequisite_depth field in dist/nodes.json, not this.

scope.description: Why this passage stands behind the other, and how far the requirement travels. "sequence" means because it is a story: the later passage continues one the earlier began, which binds those two and stops there. "foundation" means because it is an idea: the later passage uses something the earlier establishes and never re-establishes, so the requirement carries onward to anything that needs the later passage. Present on hard edges only; a soft edge constrains nothing and has nothing to pass along.

prerequisites.description: Directional: read these before this node. Core nodes may only point at core nodes (enforced by validate.mjs).

connections.description: Bidirectional enrichment links — related, not required. Declared on one side; build materializes both directions.

tradition_notes.description: Optional. Where Catholic/Orthodox/Protestant readings genuinely diverge on this passage. Neutral and factual; notes the divergence, never adjudicates it.

key_verses.description: Verse REFERENCES only (e.g. "Genesis 1:27", "Romans 8:38-39") — never verse text. The consuming app renders text from the Berean Standard Bible. These are the verses most cited when teaching the passage.

reading_time_minutes.description: Estimated careful study-reading time for the passage (~200 wpm plus study margin; law/poetry/apocalyptic read slower than narrative/epistle).

discussion_prompt.description: One open-ended reflection question answerable from the passage alone. Works across ages and traditions; engages a key theme; never yes/no.

assessment_questions.description: Exactly three questions progressing in depth: factual, interpretive, applied. All answerable from the passage.

teaching_concepts.description: 2-4 distinct teaching or apologetics concepts tied to this passage, sourced per teaching_source. Tradition-neutral above the Nicene floor.

teaching_source.description: Provenance of the teaching-layer content. "apologist.ai" = The Apologist Project's curated Fusion corpus (authoritative for the 66-book canon only); "cross-tradition" = mainstream scholarship of the traditions that hold the book, used deliberately for deuterocanonical nodes where the corpus is not the authority; "fallback" = mainstream cross-tradition understanding used because the corpus was unreachable.

completion_criteria.description: One demonstrable outcome — something the learner could explain to another person or write a short reflection on after this node.

content_density.description: How much conceptual weight the passage carries per page.

emotional_tone.description: One or two tones from the controlled list, so the UI stays clean.

comprehension_check.description: Machine-checkable mastery gate. HARD RULES: (1) each question tests the HINGE (the passage's main point), never trivia; (2) every distractor is a plausible-but-wrong READING of the passage, not a wrong fact; (3) if the question can be answered by keyword-scanning the text without understanding it, it fails; (4) options must be BALANCED in length, specificity, and confidence — a distractor is stated as fully and thoughtfully as the correct answer, so the answer is never identifiable by its shape alone (longest / most nuanced / most hedged); (5) vary the position of the correct answer across questions so answer_index is not always the same slot. answer_index is 0-based into options.

why.description: One line: why the answer is right and the plausible distractors fall short. Shown after a correct answer.

hint.description: Shown after a wrong answer. Names the specific verses to re-read and what to notice there, WITHOUT revealing the answer. It points; it does not tell. e.g. 'Read Genesis 3:1-5 again. Notice what the serpent says before he says anything about the fruit.'

from.description: First verse, e.g. '22:17'. Present on every node after the 2026-07 restructure; REQUIRED when the node shares a chapter with a sibling (verse-bounded child).

verse_span.description: Authoritative verse boundary. The id is a label; this span is the truth. BSB-verified in Phase 2B.
